lab07-s000.title: Before You Begin
lab07-s000.markdown:
**Estimated time:** 30 minutes
**What you will build:** An asset register with column types, lookups, approvals, and access controls, plus an automation that retires a selected asset with one button. ---

lab07-s001.title: The Story So Far
lab07-s001.markdown:
Harborlight's plan is complete. In this module, you will address another challenge closely related to planning.

Every planning process needs reference data: asset registers, cost center lists, product hierarchies, and employee lists. Yet responsibility for maintaining that data is often unclear. Four people can edit a shared spreadsheet, each stakeholder has a different approach, and there is no record of who changed what.

**PowerTable** is a governed data app within Fabric Planning. Without writing code, you can introduce a schema, approval workflows, row-level permissions, and audit logs to these spreadsheets.

> [!NOTE]
> This module is independent and uses a separate Plan item and dataset. If you only want to explore planning features, skip ahead to [Module 08](08-sizing-and-governance.md).
>
> **Costs:** Creating and editing PowerTable sheets are Stakeholder operations, not Planner operations. Microsoft's role documentation explicitly states that these operations no longer upgrade a session to Planner, and that Plan items containing **only PowerTable sheets** support only the Stakeholder and Viewer roles. This module therefore incurs a Stakeholder session (168 CU hours), not a Planner session. If a Planner session is already active on the same capacity, there is no additional session charge.

**Required file:** Use `Northwind-FMCG-assets-powertable-tutorial.xlsx` from [fabric-samples](https://github.com/microsoft/fabric-samples/tree/main/docs-samples/iq/plan). The workbook contains **four sheets: Assets, Employees, Locations, and Import**. In this exercise, import them into new tables in the order **Locations → Employees → Assets**. `Import` contains data for subsequent imports, so do not use it for the initial dataset.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Capacity caution:** The current Learn [prerequisites](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/overview-prerequisites) describe automatic creation of a SQL database for metadata, whereas the [FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/resources/frequently-asked-questions) says that application metadata for new Plan items is stored in OneLake. These descriptions do not agree.
>
> Before the workshop, check the target capacity and the number of available SQL databases, and arrange a dedicated storage destination for this exercise. `GEN_DB_010` indicates the capacity limit for SQL databases ([error list](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/resources/error-codes-and-resolutions)). If you reach the limit, contact the administrator or switch to an instructor demonstration. Do not delete existing Plans or databases to free up capacity.

---

lab07-s002.title: Part 1: Prepare the Environment
lab07-s002.markdown:
In this module, create a new Plan and SQL database dedicated to practicing asset management.

1. In the dedicated exercise folder, select **New item** → **SQL database**. Name the new database `fabric_plan_training` and select **Create**. If the name is already in use, ask the instructor for a new unique name and substitute it wherever `fabric_plan_training` appears below. Do not select an existing database.

   ![New SQL database dialog with fabric_plan_training entered](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-sql-create-dialog.png)

2. Wait for creation to finish. On the SQL database home page, confirm that `fabric_plan_training` appears in Explorer.

   ![Created SQL database with fabric_plan_training visible in Explorer](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-sql-created-home.png)

3. In the same dedicated exercise folder, select **New item** → **Plan**. Name the new Plan `Harborlight_Asset_Management` and select **Create**. Do not reuse an existing Plan.

   ![Creation dialog specifying Harborlight_Asset_Management and its destination](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-create-plan-dialog.png)

   ![New Plan landing page with entry points for PowerTable, Planning, and Intelligence](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-plan-landing.png)

You will configure the SQL connection when creating the first PowerTable sheet in the next part. This independent exercise does not require a connection to a planning semantic model.

> [!NOTE]
> PowerTable data is stored in a SQL database that you manage. **Set up connection** at the top of the screen provides guidance for a Viewer collaboration connection. Distinguish it from the PowerTable storage destination you are about to configure.

lab07-s003.title: Part 2: Import the Tables
lab07-s003.markdown: Import in the order **Locations → Employees → Assets** so that the lookup targets are available first. Do not use the Excel **Import** sheet for the initial dataset.

lab07-s004.markdown:

2. When **Welcome to PowerTable** appears, select **Create a New App**.

   ![Selecting Create a New App on the PowerTable welcome screen](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-powertable-create-mode.png)

3. Select the connection for a Fabric SQL database. In **Database Item**, specify the database newly created for this exercise, check **Database Name**, and select **Connect**.

   ![Database Item selected and Database Name set to fabric_plan_training](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-selected-sql-database.png)

4. When **Select Table** opens, confirm that the exercise database and `dbo` appear at the lower left. **Existing Table** is selected initially; switch to **New Table**. Set **Schema** to `dbo`, **Import Data** to **Upload File**, and **Import Type** to **Excel**.

   ![New Table selected with dbo, Upload File, and Excel configured](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-locations-excel-import-settings.png)

5. Upload `Northwind-FMCG-assets-powertable-tutorial.xlsx` under **Upload File** and select **Next**. Open the Excel sheet selector at the upper right of **Preview Data** and **select only Locations**. Clear **Assets, Employees, and Import**, and confirm **1 of 4 selected** at the upper left.

6. In the **Locations** preview, configure and check the following. Leave **Import header only** off.

   | Item | Value to set or check |
   |---|---|
   | Source Table Name | `locations` |
   | Power Table Sheet Name | `locations` |
   | Start Cell / End Cell | `A1` / `E34` |
   | Data rows / columns | **33 rows / 5 columns** |
   | First row | Location Id **1**, Location **Depot** |

   ![Configured preview with only Locations selected: 1 of 4 selected, 33 rows and 5 columns, A1:E34, and both names set to locations](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-locations-preview-configured.png)

7. Select **Next** to proceed to **Configure Table**. Use the original `Location Id` and confirm **Data Type: INT**, **Input Type: Number**, **Primary Key: checked**, **Required: checked**, and **Identity Column: unchecked**. Do not switch to automatic numbering; preserve the IDs from the source file. Leave **Enable support for Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD)** off.

   ![Configure Table showing the Location Id type, primary key, Required, and unchecked Identity Column](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-locations-schema-initial.png)

8. Select **Finish** and wait for creation to complete. When **Import progress (1 of 1 completed)** and **Created successfully** for `locations` appear, select **Done**.

   ![locations import showing 1 of 1 completed, Created successfully, and Done](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-locations-created-successfully.png)

9. In the created `locations` sheet, check **Rows: 33 / Columns: 5** in the footer. The first row is **Location Id: 1, Location: Depot, Description: Storage or in repair, Building: Main, Floor: 1**.

   ![Imported locations sheet showing 33 rows and 5 columns and the Depot row with Location Id 1](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-locations-imported-table.png)

lab07-s006.markdown:

    ![Configured Assets preview with both names set to assets, range A1:R100, 99 rows and 18 columns, and 1 of 4 selected](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-assets-preview-configured.png)

16. Select **Next** to open **Configure Table**. Confirm that the original `Asset Id` is **INT / Number**, **Primary Key and Required: checked**, and **Identity Column: unchecked**. Leave **SCD** off.

    ![Configure Table showing the Asset Id type, primary key, Required, unchecked Identity Column, and SCD off](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-assets-schema-key.png)

    Scroll down and check the columns used in the later calculation.

lab07-s007.title: Verify the Import with SQL (Optional)
lab07-s007.markdown:
After importing your own exercise data, connect to `fabric_plan_training` and run the following **SELECT-only** queries from **New Query**. Inspect the physical SQL tables and columns to verify primary keys, row counts, and references that are harder to check from the PowerTable display alone.

**Primary keys, types, Identity attributes, and column counts**

```sql
SELECT s.name AS SchemaName, t.name AS TableName,
       c.name AS PrimaryKeyColumn, ty.name AS DataType,
       c.is_nullable AS Nullable, c.is_identity AS IdentityColumn,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sys.columns c2
        WHERE c2.object_id = t.object_id) AS ColumnCount
FROM sys.tables t
JOIN sys.schemas s ON s.schema_id = t.schema_id
JOIN sys.indexes i ON i.object_id = t.object_id AND i.is_primary_key = 1
JOIN sys.index_columns ic
  ON ic.object_id = i.object_id AND ic.index_id = i.index_id
JOIN sys.columns c
  ON c.object_id = ic.object_id AND c.column_id = ic.column_id
JOIN sys.types ty ON ty.user_type_id = c.user_type_id
WHERE t.name IN (N'locations', N'employees', N'assets')
ORDER BY t.name;
```

Expected values are **33 rows / 5 columns** for `locations`, **30 rows / 9 columns** for `employees`, and **99 rows / 18 columns** for `assets`. Confirm that each primary key is `int`, with `Nullable = 0` and `IdentityColumn = 0`.

![Example SQL verification of primary keys, types, nullability, Identity attributes, and column counts for the three tables](../assets/screenshots/lab07/sql-primary-keys.png)

**Row counts and key non-nullness, uniqueness, and ranges**

```sql
SELECT N'locations' AS TableName, COUNT_BIG(*) AS TotalRows,
       COUNT_BIG([Location Id]) AS NonNullKeys,
       COUNT(DISTINCT [Location Id]) AS DistinctKeys,
       MIN([Location Id]) AS MinKey, MAX([Location Id]) AS MaxKey
FROM dbo.locations
UNION ALL
SELECT N'employees', COUNT_BIG(*), COUNT_BIG([Employee Id]),
       COUNT(DISTINCT [Employee Id]), MIN([Employee Id]), MAX([Employee Id])
FROM dbo.employees
UNION ALL
SELECT N'assets', COUNT_BIG(*), COUNT_BIG([Asset Id]),
       COUNT(DISTINCT [Asset Id]), MIN([Asset Id]), MAX([Asset Id])
FROM dbo.assets;
```

| Table | Rows | Non-null keys | Distinct keys | Key range |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `dbo.locations` | 33 | 33 | 33 | 1–33 |
| `dbo.employees` | 30 | 30 | 30 | 1–30 |
| `dbo.assets` | 99 | 99 | 99 | 1–99 |

![Example SQL verification of each table's row count, key counts, minimum, and maximum](../assets/screenshots/lab07/sql-row-key-counts.png)

**Employee and location references, and Depot**

```sql
SELECT COUNT_BIG(*) AS AssetRows,
       SUM(CASE WHEN a.[Assigned To] IS NOT NULL
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS AssignedRows,
       SUM(CASE WHEN a.[Assigned To] IS NOT NULL
                     AND e.[Employee Id] IS NULL
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS EmpOrphans,
       SUM(CASE WHEN a.Location IS NOT NULL
                     AND l.[Location Id] IS NULL
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS LocOrphans,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dbo.locations
        WHERE Location = N'Depot') AS DepotRows,
       (SELECT MIN([Location Id]) FROM dbo.locations
        WHERE Location = N'Depot') AS DepotId
FROM dbo.assets a
LEFT JOIN dbo.employees e ON e.[Employee Id] = a.[Assigned To]
LEFT JOIN dbo.locations l ON l.[Location Id] = a.Location;
```

Expected values are **AssetRows: 99 / AssignedRows: 29 / EmpOrphans: 0 / LocOrphans: 0 / DepotRows: 1 / DepotId: 1**. This check verifies stored keys and reference values; it does not mean you have created PowerTable Lookups or SQL foreign key constraints. Nor does it compare all 99 rows with the source file.

![Example SQL verification of asset references to employees and locations, and the Depot count](../assets/screenshots/lab07/sql-reference-integrity.png)

lab07-s008.title: Reopen the Plan and Verify
lab07-s008.markdown:
18. Return to the Plan and confirm the three sheets, `locations`, `employees`, and `assets`, in Explorer.

    ![Upper portion of the Plan before reload, showing three Explorer sheets and the assets table; lower portion cropped to remove an unnecessary tooltip](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-three-sheets-before-reload.png)

19. Reload the browser and confirm that all three sheets appear in **Reading** mode.

    ![Reading mode after reload, with all three sheets retained and locations showing 33 rows and 5 columns](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-reloaded-three-sheets-locations.png)

20. Select `assets` in Explorer and press **Enter** to open it if needed. Check **Rows: 99 / Columns: 18** and representative values. Switch to **Editing** at the upper right when configuring columns next.

    ![assets opened after reload, retaining 99 rows and 18 columns and representative values in Reading mode](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-reloaded-assets-reading.png)

> [!NOTE]
> **Distinguish storage destinations and save operations.** Finish during import creates SQL tables and imports data. Afterward, when you edit table values, use **Save to Database** to save them to SQL. **Save** at the upper right saves the Plan configuration. Wait for the save required for the object you changed to finish, then check the SQL values and the display in the reopened Plan.

After importing the three sheets, configure column types, Lookups, formulas, approvals, permissions, and automation.

lab07-s009.title: Part 3: Configure Columns
lab07-s009.markdown: Turn `assets` into an asset register with images and selectable inputs. Configure Logo URL, Status, Assigned To, and Location, and create the Expected EOL Date formula column.

lab07-s010.title: Open Column Settings
lab07-s010.markdown:
1. Open the `assets` sheet and switch the mode at the upper right to **Editing**. Open **Setup** → **Columns**. Select the **pencil icon** to the left of the target column to open its settings panel on the right.

   A column's **input type** and the **data type** stored in SQL are separate settings. For example, even after changing to a Lookup that displays employee names, SQL's Assigned To stores an integer employee ID.

lab07-s011.title: Display Logos as Images
lab07-s011.markdown:
2. Select the pencil icon for `Logo URL`. On the **General** tab, set **Input Type** to **Image** and select **Save**. Leave **Data Type** as the original **VARCHAR**. Do not rename the column.

   ![Logo URL input type set to Image while the SQL data type remains VARCHAR](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-p3-logo-image-settings.png)

   Logo URL in this sample contains Base64 image data beginning with `data:image`. Setting it to **Image** displays logos instead of long text strings.

   ![Upper assets table after saving, showing logos in Logo URL and Preview Changes (0); lower portion cropped to remove an unnecessary tooltip](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-p3-post-save-native-check.png)

   The footer is cropped out of the image. On your actual screen, also confirm **Rows: 99 / Columns: 18** and **Session ready**.

lab07-s012.title: Standardize Status to Four Choices
lab07-s012.markdown:
3. Select the pencil icon for `Status` and set **Input Type: Single Select** and **Values Type: Manual**. Enter the following strings in **Option** and **Label**, matching capitalization and spaces exactly.

   | Option | Label |
   |---|---|
   | Retired | Retired |
   | Available | Available |
   | In Use | In Use |
   | Under Maintenance | Under Maintenance |

   Replace **Option** and **Label** in the three existing rows with the values above. For the fourth row, select **Add**, enter `Under Maintenance`, and press **Enter** to confirm. Check that Option and Label have the same value in each row.

   ![Status configured with four strings; check both Option and Label](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-p3-status-four-value-strings.png)

   Confirm **Data Type: VARCHAR** and **Default Value: None**, then select **Save**.

lab07-s013.title: Reference Employees by ID and Display Their Names
lab07-s013.markdown:
4. Select the pencil icon for `Assigned To`, configure the following, and select **Save**.

   | Item | Setting |
   |---|---|
   | Input Type | Single Select |
   | Values Type | Lookup |
   | Lookup Schema | dbo |
   | Lookup Table | employees |
   | Lookup Key Column | Employee Id |
   | Lookup Display Column | Full Name |
   | Filter based on another column | Off |
   | Default Value | None |

   ![Assigned To linked to Employee Id and Full Name in dbo.employees](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-p3-employee-lookup-settings.png)

   Even if a Full Name column appears in the table, the original SQL column is **Assigned To**, and its stored value is the **integer Employee Id key**. You have not replaced the key with the displayed name.

   > [!NOTE]
   > The sample includes employees with identical names. Do not assume they are the same person based on name alone; compare IDs and employee codes in `employees`. **Add Hierarchy** adds a hierarchy; it is not a setting to display an employee code as a secondary label.

lab07-s014.title: Reference Locations by ID and Display Their Names
lab07-s014.markdown:
5. Select the pencil icon for `Location`, configure the following, and select **Save**.

   | Item | Setting |
   |---|---|
   | Input Type | Single Select |
   | Values Type | Lookup |
   | Lookup Schema | dbo |
   | Lookup Table | locations |
   | Lookup Key Column | Location Id |
   | Lookup Display Column | Location |
   | Filter based on another column | Off |
   | Default Value | None |

   ![Reopened Location settings after saving, showing dbo.locations, Location Id, and Location](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-p3-location-lookup-reopened.png)

   SQL retains the integer Location key, while PowerTable displays the corresponding location name. For example, **Location Id: 1** is **Depot**, **2** is **Disposed**, and **23** is **MKT-02003**.

Lookups separate display names from stored keys. Do not treat this operation alone as creating SQL foreign key constraints or configuring a condition to exclude former employees from the choices.

lab07-s015.title: Calculate Expected EOL Date
lab07-s015.markdown:
6. On the Columns screen, select **Add Formula Column** and set **Column Name** to `Expected EOL Date`. This column is not in the original XLSX, so create it as a new column. Treat it as a formula column within the sheet and leave **Create a database column** off.

   The completed formula is:

   ```text
   DATEADD([Purchase Date], (365*[Expected Lifetime In Years]))
   ```

   **Do not paste the whole formula. Enter it in this order.**

   1. Type `DATEADD(`.
   2. Press **Ctrl+Space** to open suggestions. On the **References** tab, type `Purchase` to narrow the list. Select the actual **Purchase Date** column to insert it as a reference.
   3. Type `, (365*`.
   4. Open **Ctrl+Space** → **References** again and type `Expected` to narrow the list. Select and insert the actual **Expected Lifetime In Years** column.
   5. Type `))`, confirm that both columns are bound as references, and select **Save**.

   ![Formula entry in progress, filtering by Purchase and selecting Purchase Date from References](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-p3-formula-purchase-filtered.png)

   ![Formula entry in progress, filtering by Expected and inserting Expected Lifetime In Years](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-p3-formula-lifetime-filtered.png)

   During entry, the formula is incomplete, so a red warning appears and Save is disabled. After entering both references and the closing parentheses, the warning disappeared and Save became available. In the completed screen below, referenced columns appear in green.

   ![Completed formula with two actual column references, Create a database column off, and Save enabled](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-p3-formula-bound-complete.png)

   Simply typing bracketed column names as plain text may not create correct references to the actual columns. The official documentation also instructs you to insert each column reference from the suggestions.

   **DATEADD(date, number)** adds the specified number of days to a date. This formula adds **365 × the lifetime in years, in days**. Leap days make its results differ from adding calendar years directly.

7. After selecting **Save**, wait for creation to finish. When the table shows **Rows: 99 / Columns: 19**, enter an Asset Tag in the search box. Once its row appears, scroll the table right and check the purchase date, lifetime, and Expected EOL Date. If searching resets horizontal scrolling to the left, wait for loading to finish and scroll to the right again.

   Example sample values:

   | Asset Id / Asset Tag | Purchase Date | Lifetime in years | Days added | Expected EOL Date in the UI |
   |---|---|---:|---:|---|
   | 1 / IT-1245 | 2023-08-24 | 4 | 1,460 | 2027-08-23 |
   | 99 / IT-1343 | 2026-04-28 | 5 | 1,825 | 2031-04-27 |

   ![Single IT-1245 row showing purchase date 2023-08-24, lifetime 4, and EOL 2027-08-23](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-p3-eol-asset1-ready.png)

   ![Single IT-1343 row showing purchase date 2026-04-28, lifetime 5, and EOL 2031-04-27](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-p3-eol-asset99-ready.png)

8. Select **Save** at the upper right and wait until **Saving...** disappears and Save is disabled. Reload the browser and confirm all three Explorer sheets in **Reading** mode. Open `assets` to see all **99 rows and 19 columns**.

   Open **Editing** → **Setup** → **Columns** again and check the Image, Single Select, Lookup, and Formula settings. If you are only inspecting settings, close without changing them. If a confirmation appears, close without saving new settings.

   ![Columns after reload, showing 19 columns, Image, three Single Select columns, and the new Formula column](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-p3-reloaded-columns19.png)

   ![Status after reload, retaining all four Option and Label pairs](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-p3-reloaded-status-settings.png)

   ![Location after reload, retaining dbo.locations, key Location Id, and display column Location](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-p3-reloaded-location-settings.png)

   ![Formula column reopened after reload, retaining references to Purchase Date and Expected Lifetime In Years](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-p3-reloaded-formula-settings.png)

   Check the correspondence between purchase dates, lifetimes, and EOL dates.

   ![Top portion of the table after reload, showing purchase dates, lifetimes, EOL dates, and disabled Save at the top](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-p3-reloaded-top-six-clean.png)

   With **Create a database column** off, the formula is saved within the PowerTable sheet and recalculated from source data when displayed again. To store calculated results in a physical SQL column, enable **Create a database column**.

lab07-s016.title: Part 4: Submit Changes and Verify Saving After Approval
lab07-s016.markdown:
In this exercise, try a single-level approval flow on the dedicated sample data. During training, the same account may act as requester and approver. In production, separate roles according to business responsibilities. Multi-user, multi-level, and rule-based approvals require separate design.

> [!WARNING]
> Perform the following operations only on the dedicated exercise `assets` table newly created in Part 2. Do not change existing tables or a 99-row dataset already in use. If values differ from the sample, stop and check with the instructor.

lab07-s017.title: Configure Approvals
lab07-s017.parent: Part 4: Submit Changes and Verify Saving After Approval
lab07-s017.markdown:
1. Open the `assets` sheet in `Harborlight_Asset_Management` in **Editing** mode and select **PowerTable** → **Approvals**. If the request list is open, select **Manage Approvals**.
2. Turn **Requires Approval for All Changes** **On**.
3. Set **Enable Multi Level Approval** to **Off** and **Who can Approve changes?** to **Specific users**. Add the approver designated for training and select **Save**.

![Settings with approval for all changes On and multi-level approval Off](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-approval-saved-single-level-settings.png)

> [!WARNING]
> Do not turn **Requires Approval for All Changes** **Off** intending to pause it. In the UI checked for this workshop, switching it Off displayed a confirmation to delete approval settings and Active requests. Even when interrupting the exercise, do not switch it Off; cancel the confirmation dialog. This observation does not establish that past Closed requests are physically deleted.

lab07-s018.title: Change Status and Submit a Request
lab07-s018.parent: Part 4: Submit Changes and Verify Saving After Approval
lab07-s018.markdown:
4. Select **Back to PowerTable** and enter `IT-1245` in the search box. Confirm that the result is one row with Asset Id **1**. The sample's initial values are **Full Name: blank / Location: Disposed / Status: Retired**. If they differ, do not change them; check with the instructor.
5. Select **Available** from the **Status** choices. In **Preview Changes**, confirm that exactly one row is affected and Status is the only changed column.
6. Select **Submit for Review**, enter the reason for the change in Description, and select **Submit**.

![Selecting Available from the Status choices](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-status-available-option.png)

![One-row preview showing only Status changing from Retired to Available](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-status-preview-one-row.png)

lab07-s019.title: Approve and Apply the Change
lab07-s019.parent: Part 4: Submit Changes and Verify Saving After Approval
lab07-s019.markdown:
7. Open **Approvals** → **Pending Requests**, review the request, and select **Approve**. After completion, open the request from **Closed** and confirm that it is approved.
8. Return to `assets` and confirm that **Status** for `IT-1245` is **Available**.
9. In the request's **View History**, check **Request Approved → Job Created → Request Completed**. Compare the destination table, Row Count, and Status in the corresponding **Writeback Logs**. Do not infer successful SQL writeback merely because the request moved to **Closed**. Use read-only SELECT queries to verify that the target Asset Id retains its original value before approval and becomes **Available** after approval. Also confirm that other rows have not changed. If some states do not appear on screen, do not infer missing information; record only the states you could actually verify.

![assets sheet after approval, with Status set to Available](../assets/screenshots/lab07/lab07-status-available-fields-before-restore.png)

lab07-s020.title: Restore the Original Status
lab07-s020.parent: Part 4: Submit Changes and Verify Saving After Approval
lab07-s020.markdown:
10. Change Status in the same exercise sample back to **Retired** and check the target row and changed column in **Preview Changes**. Submit the restoration through **Submit for Review** and confirm **Status: Retired** after approval.
11. Confirm that the requests created during training are complete. Do not make test changes to production data or rows outside the exercise.

Reference: [Set up PowerTable approvals, access controls, and automations](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/planning-tutorial/powertable/tutorial-8-set-up-approvals-access-controls-automations).

lab07-s021.title: Part 5: Control Access
lab07-s021.markdown:
**Data security models:** The current [PowerTable data security settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/powertable-how-to-configure-security-settings) provide two models.

| Security model | Purpose | Caution |
|---|---|---|
| **Manage Access (Legacy)** | Control adding, updating, and deleting rows and columns | Do not treat controls on editing operations as restrictions on which rows can be viewed |
| **Roles & Policies Security** | Role- and policy-based Read, Insert, Update, Delete, and static / dynamic RLS | Enabling it overrides Legacy settings. Configure it for each target database |

lab07-s022.title: Basic Exercise: Restrict Who Can Edit
lab07-s022.markdown:
1. On the **Setup** tab, select **Manage Access**. Confirm that the current model is Legacy.
2. In **Row Access**, configure the users or groups allowed to **Add**, **Update**, and **Delete**. For this exercise, consider a setup where regional staff can update their assigned assets and only asset administrators can delete them.
3. If using **Rule based access**, configure the target-row conditions and permitted users, then save.
4. Open the sheet as a different, non-administrator user. Confirm that the user can change permitted rows and cannot perform disallowed operations. **Separately record which rows the user can view.**

lab07-s023.title: Restricting Visible Rows: Roles & Policies Security
lab07-s023.markdown:
Use this route only after the instructor has checked it on the target capacity and UI in advance. Until permission design is complete, use sample data without confidential information.

1. Open **Security** on the toolbar and select the target SQL database used by PowerTable. Enable **Roles & Policies Security**.
2. Create a policy with **Add Policy**. From **Add Rule**, configure the target schema and table, permissions such as **Read** and **Update**, and filter conditions such as region or location. Insert cannot be combined in the same rule with Read, Update, Delete, or filters; create a separate rule if needed.
3. Create a role under **Roles** and associate the policy. Assign the target users under **Users**.
4. Check the **Item Baseline** inherited by unassigned users. The default is full access. Tables without rules also allow full access, so configure every table that requires protection. **Bypass Mode** prioritizes full access; do not assign it to ordinary users.
5. For dynamic RLS, map users to their scope in **User Attributes** and associate conditions using **Logged in User** with the policy. Choose the specific columns to match your organization's identity and organizational design.
6. Sign in separately as regional staff member A, regional staff member B, and an administrator. Test **which rows each can view** and **which rows each can add, update, and delete** separately. Also check unassigned-user behavior. Do not begin using a configuration if its results do not match expectations.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Do not treat the permissions of the identity configured in the database connection, existing SQL-side RLS, and PowerTable Roles & Policies as equivalent. Do not assume SQL-side RLS is automatically inherited for each signed-in user. For every actual access route, including PowerTable, other sheets referenced through From Sheets, and direct SQL connections, check viewing and updating with separate users.

lab07-s024.title: Part 6: Retire an Asset with a Button
lab07-s024.markdown: **Button-triggered automation:** Follow the official [Tutorial 8](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/planning-tutorial/powertable/tutorial-8-set-up-approvals-access-controls-automations) to process only the one row selected by the user. Scheduled automation that monitors expiration dates is outside this exercise's scope.

lab07-s025.title: Configure the Trigger and Lookup
lab07-s025.parent: Part 6: Retire an Asset with a Button
lab07-s025.markdown:
1. In the **assets** sheet, select **Setup** → **Automations** → **Create Automation**.
2. Use the pencil icon to name it `Retire Asset`, and select **When a button is clicked** as the trigger.
3. Add **Add Action** → **Find Record(s)**. Set **Schema** to `dbo`, **Table** to `locations`, and **Fetch type** to **Single Record**.
4. Under **Rules**, select **Location**, operator **is**, and value `Depot`. This retrieves the Location Id of the return destination.

lab07-s026.title: Update Only the Clicked Asset
lab07-s026.parent: Part 6: Retire an Asset with a Button
lab07-s026.markdown:
5. Add **Add Action** → **Update Record**. Set **Schema** to `dbo`, **Table** to `assets`, and **Update type** to **Single Update**.
6. Be sure to configure the following condition under **Conditions**.

   | Item | Setting |
   |---|---|
   | **Field** | **Asset Id** |
   | **Operator** | **=** |
   | **Value** | **+** → **When a button is clicked** → **Asset Id** |

   This condition limits the update to the clicked row. Do not run the automation without the Asset Id condition.

7. Under **Fields** → **Add Fields**, configure these updates.

   | Field | Update |
   |---|---|
   | **Assigned To** | **Clear Value** |
   | **Status** | **Replace Value** → `Retired` |
   | **Location** | **+** → **Find Record(s)** → **Location Id** |

8. Select **Save**, then return with **Back to Setup**.

lab07-s027.title: Add the Button and Test
lab07-s027.parent: Part 6: Retire an Asset with a Button
lab07-s027.markdown:
9. Select **PowerTable** → **Insert Column** → **Visual Column** → **Add Button Column**.
10. Set **Column Name** to `Automation`, **Label** to `Retire Asset`, **Action** to **Execute an Automation**, and **Automation** to `Retire Asset`, then save.
> [!WARNING]
> **Approvals On does not necessarily guarantee that an automation waits for approval.** With the button, settings, and executor checked in this workshop, SQL was observed to update without a new Pending request even while approvals remained On. This is an observation for that configuration, not a universal specification for all automations. Check your target configuration using dedicated sample data. If its approval route differs from expectations, stop using it and investigate.

11. Select one row from the dedicated sample newly imported for this exercise. Before running, record Asset Id, Asset Tag, Assigned To, Status, and Location. Do not run against existing 99-row data or rows outside the exercise. Select **Retire Asset** only once, then confirm **Status** is `Retired`, **Location** is `Depot`, and **Assigned To** is blank for the target row. If the display is stale, use Refresh to reload it. Do not rerun the button solely to refresh the display.
12. Open **Setup** → **Automations** → `Retire Asset` → **Run History** → **View Details**. Check the Job ID, start time, status, and displayed action results for the same run. If the screen shows the Find Record(s) output and the Asset Id passed to Update Record, also confirm that the ID matches the target row.

![Example action results in Run History's View Details; run ID and time are masked](../assets/screenshots/lab07/automation-run-details.png)

In the configuration used for this workshop, View Details displayed results for **Find Record(s)** and **Update Record**, but not the Trigger runtime fields or Find Record(s) inputs. Saved conditions are not a substitute for runtime inputs. If a field is not displayed, check both the target row's updated values and the action results that are displayed. Do not infer success from the completion notification alone. Displayed fields and behavior may vary by environment.

13. Use a read-only SQL SELECT to check the row with the same Asset Id and confirm that **Assigned To / Status / Location** after automation match the on-screen values. Also confirm that other rows were not updated. Do not restore values with a direct SQL UPDATE.
14. Open **Record Details** for the same key and restore the three fields recorded before execution. In Preview, confirm that only the one target row and those three fields change, then create a new request. After the approver approves it, Refresh and check the table values, then compare the same SQL key with a read-only SELECT. Do not restore by turning approval settings Off or changing SQL directly.

lab07-s028.title: Limits to Consider During Design
lab07-s028.parent: Part 6: Retire an Asset with a Button
lab07-s028.markdown:
| Limit applies to | Maximum |
|---|---|
| Records retrieved by **Find Action** | Only the first **1,000 records** |
| Repeating-group iterations | First **1,000 items** |
| Chained trigger depth | **2 levels**, including the initial trigger |
| Database-trigger writeback | **10 records per trigger type** |
| Multi-record operations | Not supported in subsequent actions; single-record operations only |

The 10-record limit concerns **database triggers** for Create Record, Update Record, Delete Record, and Form Submission. If more than 10 records are involved, none of them starts a job; the system does not simply process the first 10. Do not confuse this with the **button trigger** in this exercise. When designing bulk processing, check the [current limitations](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/overview-limitations) and run history.

Each successful automation job incurs **2 CU**, using the notation in the official [billing documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/resources/billing-fabric-plan). Failed jobs are not billed. This notation differs from session CU hours, so do not add this value directly as CU hours.

lab07-s029.title: Part 7: Check Audit Logs
lab07-s029.markdown:
1. In the **assets** sheet, select **View audit logs**.

Check the automation changes and the restoration in step 14 separately. Filter to the target row. Where displayed, inspect each column's old / new values and **Source Type**, and compare them with the corresponding operation in Run History or approval History. Trace requests, Jobs, and audit entries using fields actually visible on screen. Do not infer undisplayed inputs or omitted timestamps. Moving to **Closed** alone does not establish successful SQL writeback. Audit log contents and retention may vary with settings and environment.

If an audit row displays **Request ID**, compare it with the same request's ID. Otherwise, select an audit row matching the target Asset Id, column name, old / new values, and operator, and verify that its **Transaction ID** matches the **Job ID** shown in **View History**. If you cannot actually verify those IDs as a shared key, do not link entries based solely on similar times or the same Status. Record the audit event and request / Job as separately verified evidence. Do not combine the automation and restoration into the history of one operation.

---

lab07-s030.title: Module Outcomes
lab07-s030.markdown: In this module, you use dedicated sample data to learn PowerTable imports, column configuration, Lookups, formula columns, approvals, access controls, and automation. Make changes only to data created specifically for training; do not modify data outside the exercise.

lab07-s031.title: Knowledge Check
lab07-s031.markdown:
1. Why must you enter a formula column's formula manually instead of pasting it?
2. In a separate automation triggered by database updates, updating 40 rows at once did not start a job. Why?
3. You configured the update scope for regional IT staff. Is that alone enough to conclude that they cannot view rows for other locations?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Column references are bound during entry. In pasted text, references to actual columns are not resolved, and the formula stops working without an explicit error.
2. Database-trigger writeback is limited to 10 records per trigger type. If the limit is exceeded, the entire automation is skipped rather than partially processed.
3. No. Legacy update permissions and viewing scope are separate. To restrict visible rows as well, check Read, RLS, Item Baseline, tables without rules, and any Bypass in Roles & Policies Security. Verify viewing and changes separately with another user.

</details>
